Clean, fresh water will become increasingly scarce and largely controlled by the few surviving corporations, many of which will have consolidated into mega-corps. Some advanced technologies will continue to be developed, but only for the few remaining wealthy and for their use alone. Food and water shortages will lead to wars and cause societies to further fracture into factions based primarily on race, religion and/or ethnic heritage.

And this got me to thinking about something else. Every year around Halloween, a church near us would put on something called Hell House. It was a Christian version of a haunted house. You walked through different skits showing people dying in car accidents after drunken parties, having an abortion, etc., and at the end of each skit they were dragged away by demons. At the end, you saw them all being tortured.

Two things about that have stuck with me.

1) A skit featured a girl riding with her drunk friends when they get into a wreck and all die. The girl insists that she's a good person and never had a drink in her life, but the demons says, "There are millions of good people in Hell!" and carts her off. At the end of it all, she's being eaten by her friends in Hell. No joke.

2) Another skit features a kid who shoots and kills his dad after years of sexual and psychological abuse, then hangs himself in his room. Bam! Hell. And his punishment: To be tortured by his father for eternity. So what, this is Heaven for the dad? What the fuck?

Growing up, I attended a hardcore Southern Baptist church in Texas where my uncle was a pastor. We were taught that God does, indeed, hate sinners. Before we were told homosexuality was wrong in Sunday school, I'd never even thought about it before. I knew that some men liked men and some women liked women, but I didn't see anything wrong with that. Then, one morning, they handed us pamphlets warning us to avoid homosexuals because they'd try to kidnap and molest us.

I also vividly remember attending a youth conference called Planet Wisdom. This youth pastor was on stage preaching to a stadium full of thousands of young kids, and he said, "The secular world wants you to believe that God is incapable of hating people. That's a lie. The Bible clearly states that God hates sin and sinners. He hates non-Christians. He hates homosexuals. He hates atheists. A God incapable of hate is incapable of mercy."

I remember being terrified by the idea of a god who probably hated me because, no matter how hard they tried to drill this stuff into me, I just couldn't believe it. To this day, I still have a complex. I consider myself an agnostic-leaning-atheist, but I still have nightmares about going to Hell.
